authorizedBy: NOT YET AUTHORIZED FOR PRODUCTION. The founder authorized implementation of Project Drive on 2026-09-02, but production data remains an explicit founder gate. This review receipt authorizes local and CI application only; no tasks-migration-execution/1 receipt exists for 0028.
reviewedBy: Codex, Project Drive WP-3 implementation review, 2026-09-02
authorizationSource: Project Drive PROJECT.md WP-3 and the 2026-09-02 implementation instruction. Scope is additive schema only: immutable provider-connection and workspace-storage generations, exact Drive grant receipts, three resource columns, and no remote database execution.

migrations.risk: low-medium at apply time. The migration creates three empty tables and eight named indexes, then adds three columns to resources. Existing resources receive storage='signal'; no existing value is deleted or rewritten. A cross-field check prevents a Drive resource without a storage generation and prevents a Signal-native resource from claiming one. Dedicated immutable ids prevent owner A to B to A, a different Drive reconnect, or a replacement missing folder from overwriting prior credential, folder or permission evidence. Every custody foreign key restricts deletion, forcing lifecycle code to revoke and clean explicitly before removing a user, workspace, connection, generation or grant. The residual risk begins only after runtime use: these rows contain encrypted credential custody, Drive folder identity and exact revocation ids, so deleting them casually would make cleanup less reliable even though no Drive bytes are stored here.
migrations.rollbackPlan: Before any live connection exists: drop idx_resources_workspace_storage_generation, drop the resources stored_path, storage_generation_id and storage columns, then drop idx_drive_folder_grants_workspace_generation and drive_folder_grants; drop the four workspace_storage indexes and workspace_storage; drop the two provider_connections indexes and provider_connections. After any connection or grant exists, do not use a schema-only rollback: first disable Drive writes, revoke every recorded permission and provider token, preserve the resource-to-generation audit relation, then roll forward or execute a separately reviewed data migration. A table drop after use would destroy the exact permission ids needed to remove access at Google.
postconditions: resources has storage, storage_generation_id and stored_path; every pre-existing row remains storage='signal'
provider_connections is immutable by id, identifies Drive accounts by Drive User.permissionId, and permits at most one current credential generation per user and provider
workspace_storage is immutable by id and permits at most one current folder generation per workspace
drive_folder_grants keys each permission receipt to its exact storage generation and member
owner A to B to A and same-owner replacement folders can retain distinct historical generations
resource generation lookups are indexed and reference workspace_storage
custody foreign keys restrict deletion rather than silently cascading or nulling repair evidence
resource storage/generation coupling and all JSON, state, role, boolean and key-version constraints exist
